title: Overheating: heat stroke (Earth reference, no space data)

steps.text: Suspect heat stroke in a hot environment if the crewmember has a raised core temperature, confusion, agitation, disorientation, seizures or does not respond.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
source.section: Concise guidelines for clinical practice, Heat stroke

steps.text: Move them away from the heat source and start passive cooling: remove extra clothing and move them to a cooler place.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
source.section: Concise guidelines for clinical practice, Heat stroke, passive cooling

steps.text: If their core temperature is above 40 °C, start active cooling at once with any method you have.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
source.section: Concise guidelines for clinical practice, Heat stroke, active cooling

steps.text: If you cannot measure core temperature, keep cooling for 15 minutes or until the neurological symptoms resolve, whichever comes first.

source.guideline: Djärv T, Rogers J, Semeraro F, et al. European Resuscitation Council Guidelines 2025 First Aid. Resuscitation. 2025;215:110752. doi:10.1016/j.resuscitation.2025.110752 (Earth reference, no space data)
